content: 1. A Registered Design Professional refers to an individual who is officially registered or licensed to practice their specific design profession, as defined by the statutory requirements of professional registration laws in the state or jurisdiction where the project is to be constructed. 2. A Regulatory Authority is a local, state, federal, or equivalent international enforcement body or authorized representative that has jurisdiction over food processing, transportation, warehousing, or other food establishments. 3. Removable describes an object that can be detached from the main unit using simple tools such as a screwdriver, pliers, or an open-end wrench. 4. A Reportable AGE Case (as per VSP definition) involves acute gastroenteritis (AGE) with specific characteristics: Diarrhea: Three or more episodes of loose stools within a 24-hour period or an amount above normal for the individual (e.g., individuals with underlying medical conditions), OR Vomiting accompanied by at least one additional symptom, such as one or more episodes of loose stools in a 24-hour period, abdominal cramps, headache, muscle aches, or fever (temperature ≥38°C), AND The case must be reported to the vessel's master, medical staff, or other designated personnel by a passenger or crew member. 5. Nausea, while a common symptom of AGE, is specifically excluded from this definition to avoid misclassifying seasickness (nausea and vomiting) as acute gastroenteritis. 6. A Restricted-Use Pesticide is a pesticide product containing active ingredients classified under 40 CFR 152.175 as restricted-use pesticides. These are limited to application by or under the direct supervision of a certified applicator. 7. A Sanitizer refers to chemical or physical agents that reduce microbial contamination levels on inanimate environmental surfaces. 8. There are two classes of sanitizers: Sanitizers for non-food-contact surfaces: These must achieve a 99.9% (3-log) reduction of the target microorganism within 5 minutes of contact time, as per EPA standards. Sanitizers for food-contact surfaces: These must achieve a 99.999% (5-log) reduction of the target microorganism within 30 seconds, as per EPA standards. 9. Sanitization is the application of cumulative heat or chemicals to cleaned food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces, which, when evaluated for efficacy, provide a sufficient reduction of pathogens. 10. A Scupper is a conduit or collection basin designed to channel liquid runoff to a deck drain. 11. A Sealant is a material used to fill seams. 12.8 millimeters (1/32 inch) but less than 3 millimeters (1/8 inch). 13. Sewage refers to liquid waste containing animal or vegetable matter in suspension or solution, which may also include liquids containing chemicals in solution. 14. Shellstock refers to raw, in-shell molluscan shellfish. 15. Shucked Shellfish are molluscan shellfish with one or both shells removed. 16. Single-Service Articles include tableware, carry-out utensils, and other items such as bags, containers, placemats, stirrers, straws, toothpicks, and wrappers designed for one-time, one-person use. 17. Single-Use Articles are utensils and bulk food containers designed for one-time use and disposal. Examples include wax paper, butcher paper, plastic wrap, formed aluminum food containers, jars, plastic tubs or buckets, bread wrappers, pickle barrels, ketchup bottles, and large cans that do not meet material, durability, strength, and cleanability specifications. 18. Slacking is the process of moderating the temperature of food, such as allowing it to gradually increase from -23°C (-10°F) to -4°C (25°F), in preparation for deep-fat frying or to facilitate even heat penetration during the cooking of previously block-frozen food, such as spinach. 19. A Smooth surface is defined as: For food-contact surfaces: A surface free of pits and inclusions, with cleanability equal to or exceeding that of 100-grit stainless steel. For non-food-contact surfaces: A surface of equipment equal to commercial-grade hot-rolled steel, free of visible scale. For decks, bulkheads, or deckheads: An even or level surface with no roughness or projections that would make cleaning difficult. 20. A Spa Pool is a potable water or saltwater-supplied pool with characteristics similar to a whirlpool spa, including: Water temperatures of 30°C to 40°C (86°F to 104°F), Bubbling, jetted, or sprayed water effects that break at or above the water surface, A depth of more than 1 meter (3 feet), and A tub volume exceeding 6 tons of water. 21. 22. A Spray Pad is a play and water contact area designed to have no standing water. 23. A Suction Fitting is a fitting in a recreational water facility that operates under direct suction, drawing water through a pump. 24. A Swimming Pool is a recreational water facility with a depth greater than 1 meter. This definition excludes spa pools that meet this depth. 25. Table-Mounted Equipment refers to equipment that is not portable and is designed to be mounted off the floor on a table, counter, or shelf. 26. Tableware includes eating, drinking, and serving utensils for table use, such as flatware (forks, knives, spoons), hollowware (bowls, cups, serving dishes, tumblers), and plates. 27. Technical Water refers to water that has not been chlorinated or pH-controlled onboard a vessel. It originates from bunkering, condensate collection processes, or seawater processed through evaporators or reverse osmosis plants and is intended for storage and use in the technical water system. 28. A Temperature-Measuring Device (TMD) is a thermometer, thermocouple, thermistor, or other device that indicates the temperature of food, air, or water, numerically scaled in Celsius and/or Fahrenheit. 29. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) is synonymous with Potentially Hazardous Food (PHF). 30. Transmission of Infection refers to any mechanism by which an infectious agent spreads from a source or reservoir to another person. These mechanisms include: Direct transmission: Immediate transfer of infectious agents to a receptive portal of entry, allowing human or animal infection. Indirect transmission: Transfer of infectious agents via an intermediate item, organism, means, or process to a susceptible host, resulting in disease. This includes airborne, foodborne, waterborne, vehicleborne (e.g., fomites), and vectorborne modes of transmission. 31. Turnover refers to the circulation of a quantity of water equal to the pool volume through the recirculation system. For baby-only water facilities, the entire water volume must pass through all parts of the system, including filtration, secondary ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, and halogenation, once every 30 minutes. 32. A Utensil is a food-contact implement or container used in storing, preparing, transporting, dispensing, selling, or serving food. Examples include kitchenware or tableware (multiservice, single-service, or single-use), gloves used in contact with food, food temperature-measuring devices, and probe-type price or identification tags used in contact with food. 33. A Utility Sink is any sink located in a food service area that is not intended for handwashing or warewashing. 34. A Variance is a written document issued by the Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) that authorizes a modification or waiver of one or more requirements of the guidelines if, in the opinion of the VSP, a health-related justification is provided.
